title: Are procedural games generative AI?
author: yuripourre
selftext:
I am working on this game for more than 1000 hours. And got a lot of mixed feedback from the fact I used AI to code it.

Because the entire game is procedural some people think it's an AI slop but some people are fine since it's code even though they hate AI.

How would you even disclose that on Steam/Itch since the graphics are user facing but generated with code??

I tried to improve the graphics since people called it AI slop but I think for majority of games doesn't matter because I used AI.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/5172840/Low\_Space\_Race/

comments.author: Fantastic-Jeweler781
comments.body: Do not pay attention to the AI haters who never build anything and just critize

replies.author: yuripourre
replies.body: Yeah, I always dreamed of being a game developer and now I have a tool that allows me to move fast. It's hard not to use it.

replies.author: NickMotionless
replies.body: Same here, man. I always dreamed of making my own game and now it's possible and easier than ever. Is it going to be my exact vision or my own art? Maybe not, but it will be damn close and I will fine-tune every small, minute detail until I get it how I like it.

replies.author: WarmWombat
replies.body:
How would you know if they’ve ever built anything?  
The negative view against AI is because of the perceived lack of skill and effort that goes into the development. This can directly impact on the perceived value as well, which is relevant to any kind of business in some form or another.

It is up to the person developing with AI to provide context and explain the effort that went in. Like it or not, if everyone snotnose kid with access to generative AI can spit out slop, why should others be interested in it?

It will be harder to market your game using AI assistance. Respect your end users by disclosing the extent you used it, and let then make up their own minds.

If you are going to treat them as ‘AI haters’, you probably don’t have the skill in the first place and you will likely fail.

replies.author: yuripourre
replies.body:
That's the thing, I could make this game without using AI it would just take a few years.

I understand people that hate AI for the fact it steals art, knowledge and anything else. But in this case everything that is visible is based on mathematical formulas, noise algorithms, image processing.

Is this the same?

comments.author: ChadSexman
comments.body:
I feel it’s ethical to disclose AI code if asked, but Steam’s disclosure is only required for generated content that can be seen or heard (models, textures, music, effects, etc).

Procedural generation is not typically lumped into “generative AI”.

replies.author: yuripourre
replies.body: I get it but, in this case the textures, the models they are all generated by code when the game starts. And it is user facing. Should I disclose this?

replies.author: ChadSexman
replies.body:
In this scenario, I’d ask if you used AI to generate the code which generates the models?

If yes, then I think it’s ethical to disclose AI was used to generate the models. I wouldn’t expect players to understand or care about the one layer of abstraction.

replies.author: yuripourre
replies.body:
Yes, I used AI to generate the code that generates the models when the game starts. There are no asset files.

The models are basically primitives, cubes, capsules, pyramids, it's not like it was trained with stolen art.

I don't know how to write this down.

replies.author: ChadSexman
replies.body: You’re over thinking it. If people are reading the disclosure then they are already thinking in binary. I’d go with “AI was used to generate texture, models, and …”

replies.author: yuripourre
replies.body: Good point!

replies.author: yuripourre
replies.body: I am afraid people that have no idea what it means can skip it. I wish I could explain this in a simpler way.

replies.author: I_pee_in_shower
replies.body: Are you using an AI model to generate the models if you’re using a procedure that was generated by an AI tool then it’s procedural code not generative code

comments.author: Toastti

replies.author: yuripourre

I mean, it's a $8 game, what do people expect? F-ZERO?

comments.author: thevisitor_earth
comments.body: AI is generating more and more these of them these days, but they're not generative AI. Hah.

comments.author: Mother_Tifa
comments.body: Using AI to help with coding doesn't automatically make the entire game AI-generated. The actual gameplay, design decisions, and development effort still matter

replies.author: yuripourre
replies.body: I agree, but more and more I think people are becoming very binary about it.

comments.author: FallenWyvern
comments.body:
Ok but that's a design choice: making a game fit 1.44 mb. 

What I said was that someone could make that game, without AI, and without it taking years. Of course that game would be differently designed from yours: they'd pick up the skill they need to do the next step, until the game is built.

However a game that uses proc-gen, if you're learning it by hand and coding it out, yeah that is a *discipline* and it CAN take years. Like the game kkreiger is a whole fps that fits in something like 800 kilobyes. 

And some people who don't use AI would just find the maths online, copy/paste them and maybe tweak it for their "first time" proc gen game. Which is, effectively, what claude did here. The only difference is Claude (or whatever agent was used) has digested everything published to the internet regarding that topic, meaning you skipped months learning those maths.

I'm not saying anything about your game. I think, personally, it looks good and I'm *very* anti-ai. Like I won't be buying it, but you directed your agent in a way that seems to have created a very competent game. 

I also appreciate your disclosure of AI, because I don't think you *had* to. Valve said ai written code doesn't need disclosure, only assets that are player facing that were generated using an LLM. Like, if you have code that generates a FFT to make water with waves, the water and it's texture is just maths, in the same way that the damage from a projectile in a FPS game is maths. No need for disclosure but I like that you did.

replies.author: yuripourre
replies.body:
Yes, the reason I chose to make the game that fits on a floppy disk was because of a competition.

I think you are overestimating (a lot) the amount of work needed to create those scenes/landscapes procedurally. It took me weeks to make everything look right:

Not only geometries, UVs, Textures, (normal, bump emissive) maps and rules to place them in the stage.

Or maybe I am just very dumb for not checking those websites you mentioned before trying to implement myself or maybe is a harness/prompt problem. I confess, I don't use any skills or MCPs maybe that's why?

.kkrieger was 96kb and the geometries of stages and the UI are very simplistic. It's definitely impressive for the size but shows how hard is to create complex geometries procedurally.

replies.author: FallenWyvern
replies.body:
I think perhaps I'm not communicating properly:

I want to say *congratulations* on what you've done. You've made something, and as anti-ai as I want to be, I can't deny that this shows YOUR vision. Nothing about this would read AI to me (which is why I appreciate your work).

I *also* want to say learning to code isn't a mystical process. That it's gradual and for someone with the time to want to learn the craft, they can do so. It's a multi-discipline thing. You can learn to code, but that isn't art, sound, design, etc.

Also note .kkrieger was made in 2004, so yeah it's gonna be more simplistic. But the underlying procedural fundementals are the same.

**TLDR:** I'm not saying you did anything wrong, or that your game isn't a game. What I am saying is that people *can* do all this and it doesn't take years to learn. It takes years to *master* but that's a different statement all together.

replies.author: yuripourre
replies.body:
I see what you mean now. I agree that learning how to code does not need years of study!

When I mentioned about overestimating is because I had to develop my own techniques to make the game look better AND fit on a floppy disk. I sincerely don't think someone that don't code for many years could do that. But maybe I am just thinking I am better than I really am.

Also, not sure if you agree with me but in a game programming is usually the easy/quick part so in this game there is still a lot that could be done in terms of visuals.

comments.author: I_pee_in_shower
comments.body: In order for a game to be procedural, you need to code a tool or routine. If you used code assistant tools, and you’re required to disclose that then disclose it. I would never code a procedural tool by hand, anymore, and I think it’s done to have to disclose AI code assistance at this stage. But to answer your question, procedural code is not generative code the routine that creates it might’ve been created from generative AI, but a procedure is deterministic and generative AI isn’t.

replies.author: Brettinabox
replies.body: Yup, lately ive separated the term into generative and analytical. AI just doesnt create out of thin air so it matters what one feeds into it for the results  aka prompts.
